svg.title: From Case Screening to Documented Kinship
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-document-the-right-family; chapter number: 1; title: From Case Screening to Documented Kinship; subtitle: Check the opportunity before extending the family search.; caption: Leslie Lawson recommends preliminary case screening; John and Char check funds and competing claims; HeirSearch and PBI Research Services describe kinship verification.; assumptions note: Leslie Lawson, John and Char, HeirSearch, Daniel Curran, and PBI Research Services describe separate practices. This sequence combines those practices without implying a shared firm, fee model, or guaranteed recovery.; note: PBI Research Services reports finding at least one relative over 95% of the time, not proving every beneficiary's entitlement. Daniel Curran's charity-will example demonstrates that research can still be written off.; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Screen the assignment; value: Step 1; detail: Leslie Lawson recommends a preliminary hour to assess whether the case fits the researcher's skills.; step: 02; label: Confirm funds and case activity; value: Step 2; detail: John and Char visit the courthouse to check other claimants and confirm that the money remains.; step: 03; label: Resolve prior kin and any will; value: Step 3; detail: HeirSearch requires excluding living heirs at the prior level before moving up the chart. Daniel Curran's cases show how half siblings or a newly found will can displace a wider-family search.; step: 04; label: Corroborate each relationship; value: Step 4; detail: PBI Research Services marks a relationship possible with one source and confirmed with two sources, and adds a second reviewer.; step: 05; label: Deliver the documented finding; value: Step 5; detail: Lawson uses reusable report and citation templates. PBI Research Services supplies PDF and Excel reports for reading, retention, and client-system use.
